reason: Chiseling planks seems like a useful start for building the printing press.
expectation: I expect to shape the planks into a component for the press, though its exact form is unclear.

alternatives.reason: Stone and rope might make a weight for the clock, but I'll start with the press.

effect: The shaped planks became a printing block, suggesting iron can help build the press.
reaction: The result makes sense as a starting point for printing.
reason: Combine the printing block with iron to advance the press.
expectation: I expect a printing press or another press component, though the exact result is unclear.

alternatives.reason: Stone and rope may make a clock weight, but I want to continue the press first.

effect: The printing press is complete, and the new goal is to print a page.
reaction: The screw and plate explanation makes the press mechanism clear.
reason: Use paper with the press to pursue the new goal.
expectation: I expect a printed page, though ink may still be needed.

alternatives.reason: Charcoal and water might make ink, but I will try the offered press and paper combination first.

effect: The paper is in place, but the block still needs ink before printing.
reaction: The explanation makes the remaining step clear.
reason: Charcoal and water seem likely to make ink for the press.
expectation: I expect a dark ink mixture, though I don't know its exact name.

alternatives.reason: Stone and rope may help with the clock, but I want to finish printing first.

effect: Charcoal and water made ink, so I can now use it with the prepared press.
reaction: The result was expected and fits the printing task.
reason: Add the ink to the prepared press to pursue the printed page goal.
expectation: I expect the press to produce a printed page.

alternatives.reason: Stone and rope may help make the clock, but I want to finish printing first.

effect: The inked press produced printed pages and completed the printing goal; the clock remains.
reaction: Seeing the same illustration copied onto multiple sheets makes the press's purpose tangible.
reason: Stone and rope are the only offered combination, and they may form a weight for the clock.
expectation: I expect a suspended weight or pendulum component, though its exact form is uncertain.

effect: Stone and rope made a pendulum, which can now be combined with the wooden gear for the clock.
reaction: The result fits the expected suspended component.
reason: Combine the pendulum and gear to advance the remaining clock goal; it is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect a clock or a clock mechanism, though the exact result is uncertain.

effect: The pendulum and gear made clockwork; planks can now complete or house the mechanism.
reaction: The mechanism is a sensible intermediate step.
reason: Combine the clockwork with planks to pursue the clock goal; it is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect a clock, perhaps with a wooden case.

effect: The planks completed the clock, and both chapter goals are now finished.
reaction: The explanation of the gears counting pendulum swings made the finished clock satisfying.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the printing press was most worthwhile because its explanation made the screw-and-plate mechanism clear.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making ink was predictable once the press said it needed ink, though it served a clear purpose.

surprise.text: Combining paper with the press prepared an uninked press rather than immediately producing a page.

arbitrary.text: No action felt entirely arbitrary, though combining the pendulum and gear into clockwork left the details of the mechanism unexplained.

continue.text: I would choose to continue for another chapter to see more mechanisms explained, especially if they offer the same tangible detail as the printing press.
